displayTitle: The Mézard–Parisi formula for diluted spin glasses

scope.note: Statement scope reviewed against the pinned main theorem and corollaries: Poisson-diluted Ising models of fixed even arity with factorization, positivity and first-moment integrability. The limiting expected log partition function per spin equals the infimum over all finite hierarchy depths and trial laws. Includes Viana–Bray, symmetric even-spin interactions and weighted soft even-K SAT. Resolves the Panchenko–Talagrand equality conjecture for this class; does not cover every diluted model or odd-K SAT. No attainment or physical Gibbs-state hierarchy is asserted. This is a statement review, not proof verification.

originalQuestion: Mézard and Parisi proposed a one-step cavity description for the fixed-connectivity Bethe-lattice spin glass. Panchenko and Talagrand subsequently asked whether the infimum of their finite-level trial pressure bounds equals the thermodynamic pressure in their Poisson even-arity class.
modernQuestion: For the specified Poisson-diluted Ising models, does lim_{N→∞} N⁻¹ E log Z_N equal inf_{r≥0} Φ_r, with Φ_r optimizing the cavity functional at finite hierarchy depth r?
questionDifference: The 2000–2001 cavity picture concerns fixed connectivity and a one-step approximation. The 2004 equality conjecture supplies a precise Poisson model and optimization over every finite depth. The reported theorem retains that class with only first moments. An exact formula over general invariant spin distributions is distinct from reduction to this specific hierarchy.

firstFormulation.label: 18 May 2004: explicit variational equality in the inspected preprint

attribution: The name credits Marc Mézard and Giorgio Parisi’s physical cavity picture. The precise equality studied here is printed after Theorem 4 of Panchenko and Talagrand’s 2004 paper. Viana and Bray supplied an earlier diluted model; Franz and Leone proved selected interpolation bounds. Panchenko later developed the spin-distribution and finite-hierarchy branches. Biswas, Chen and Sen obtained formulas in replica-symmetric regimes. These contributions address different models or steps; this is a selected history, without an exhaustive priority claim.

questionPlainLanguage: Imagine many two-state spins connected by a sparse random network. Some interactions favor agreement, others favor opposition. Can a hierarchy of local spin preferences give the exact weighted count of all arrangements per spin as the network grows?
questionSummary: Can local preferences describe a whole disordered system?
claimSummary: the hierarchical formula for a stated even-arity class
questionFormal:
For spins $\sigma_i\in\{-1,+1\}$, let $M_N\sim\operatorname{Poisson}(\alpha N)$ and sample interaction indices independently and uniformly from $\{1,\ldots,N\}$, with replacement. Fix even $p\ge2$ and independent interaction and field copies:

$$
\begin{aligned}
-H_N(\sigma)&=\sum_{k=1}^{M_N}\theta_k(\sigma_{i_{1,k}},\ldots,\sigma_{i_{p,k}})\\
&\quad+\sum_{i=1}^{N}h_i\sigma_i,\\
Z_N&=\sum_{\sigma\in\{-1,+1\}^N}e^{-H_N(\sigma)}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Assume $\mathbb E\max_s|\theta(s)|+\mathbb E|h|<\infty$ and $e^{\theta(s)}=a(1+b\prod_{\ell=1}^p f_\ell(s_\ell))$, with $a>0$, independent identically distributed $f_\ell$, $b$ independent of them, $|b\prod f_\ell(s_\ell)|<1$ almost surely, and finite $\mathbb E(-b)^n\ge0$ for every $n\ge1$. The claimed equality is

$$
\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\mathbb E\log Z_N
=\inf_{r\ge0}\Phi_r.
$$

Here $\Phi_r$ is the optimized cavity trial pressure at finite depth $r$, including zero. The trial functional combines a new-site term with an interaction correction. Higher levels sample distributions of message distributions, with parameters $0<m_1<\cdots<m_r<1$. The [model section](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/fd4aeeb2ee4fc729c18d98444fed42fd0529eeeb/preprints/The-Mezard-Parisi-formula-for-diluted-spin-glasses-September-23-2026/build/sections/model.tex) defines it completely.

The left side is **pressure**. With inverse temperature $\beta$ included in the interactions, physical free energy per spin is its negative divided by $\beta$. The infimum need not be attained at finite depth.
whyItMatters:
A spin glass turns simple local rules into a difficult global counting problem. Some spins prefer to align; others prefer to oppose one another. Loops can make these preferences incompatible, leaving many competing arrangements. The partition function weights every arrangement by its energy, and its logarithm per spin controls the thermodynamic description.

Dilution keeps the average number of interactions per spin finite. Local randomness persists as the system grows, so a single average preference can miss important structure. The cavity method encodes local preferences as messages and lets their distributions vary between states. Establishing an exact formula would turn this physical description into a mathematical characterization. Related sparse interaction models also describe random constraint problems, connecting the question to combinatorial optimization.
illustrativeExample: This fixed triangle has three spins and three antiferromagnetic bonds of strength $J=-1$, with no external field. Every bond prefers opposite signs. Its energy is $H=\sigma_A\sigma_B+\sigma_B\sigma_C+\sigma_C\sigma_A$, so its eight assignments give $Z(\beta)=6e^\beta+2e^{-3\beta}$. It illustrates frustration and weighted counting, not the Poisson model or its limiting formula.
historicalHook: Knowing what every neighbor wants still may not tell you how the whole system behaves.
whatAIClaims:
OpenAI reports the exact equality

$$
\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\mathbb E\log Z_N
=\inf_{r\ge0}\Phi_r
$$

for the Poisson-diluted even-arity Ising class defined above. It identifies the optimal hierarchical trial pressure with the thermodynamic pressure, resolving the Panchenko–Talagrand equality for this class. Only first moments of the interaction and external field are required.

Examples include Viana–Bray, symmetric diluted even-spin interactions, and weighted soft even-$K$ SAT at positive temperature. The consequences section also reports a ground-state variational limit, taking system size to infinity before inverse temperature tends to infinity.

The manuscript uses auxiliary finite trees and averaged control of multioverlaps. It does not assume a hierarchical organization of physical Gibbs states.
whatRemainsOpen: The claim requires the specified factorization, positivity and even arity. It does not give a formula for every diluted spin glass, every graph ensemble, or odd-K SAT such as 3-SAT. Optimizing over all finite depths does not assert a minimizer at one finite depth or construct a limiting infinite-depth Gibbs state. An exact characterization also does not by itself supply an efficient numerical algorithm. Independent assessment and acceptance of the proof are outside this historical account.
